question.worked_solution:
The "square of a difference" formula states that

$$
{f}^{2}-2af+{a}^{2}=(f-a)^{2}.
$$

We will use this formula to factor the given trinomial. Our trinomial is

$$
-24f+144+{f}^{2}={f}^{2}-24f+144
$$

First, we write the constant term as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{2}-24f+{12}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we factor a $2$ out of the linear term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{2}-2\cdot 12f+{12}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we factor the trinomial using the square of difference formula with $a=12.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(f-12)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
